    tsdst.mcmc.adaptive_mcmc¶

    tsdst.mcmc.adaptive_mcmc(start, niter, lpost, postArgs=None, options=None)[source]¶

    Run Adaptive Mixture Metropolis with an updated proposal covariance.

    This implementation follows the adaptive covariance approach associated with Haario and Rosenthal. A small fixed normal proposal is mixed with a normal proposal based on the accumulated chain covariance.

    Parameters:
    startnumpy.ndarray

    Initial parameter vector on the scale used by lpost.

    niterint

    Number of samples, including the initial state.

    lpostcallable

    Log posterior on the sampled parameter scale. The sampler uses normal random-walk proposals and a Metropolis acceptance ratio.

    postArgsdict, optional

    Keyword arguments passed to lpost. The default is None.

    optionsdict, optional

    Sampler options. beta is the probability of selecting the small fixed proposal, default 0.05. progress controls the progress display. prev_vals resumes stored chol2, sumx, and prev_i state from an earlier run. These options belong in options, rather than postArgs.

    Returns:
    resultdict

    parameters contains the sampled parameter matrix. prev_vals contains the accumulated state needed to continue the chain.

    Notes

    With d parameters and accumulated sample covariance Sigma_n, the proposal mixture is

    \[Q_n(x, \cdot) = (1-\beta)N(x, 2.38^2\Sigma_n/d) + \beta N(x, 0.1^2 I_d/d).\]

    A uniform draw selects the component. When U < beta, the sampler uses the small fixed component; otherwise it uses the adaptive component. This selection samples the mixture directly without inverting a mixture CDF. The initial 2*d samples use the small proposal while covariance state is initialized.

    For a matrix X containing accumulated draws and column mean mu, sample covariance can be written as

    \[\left(X^T X/n - \mu^T\mu\right)n/(n-1).\]

    The code updates the Cholesky factor of the accumulated cross-product matrix with cholupdate. A rank-one downdate removes the mean contribution before applying the 2.38/sqrt(d) proposal scale. The stored running sum and sample count allow this calculation to continue across runs.
